title: Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome — Three Years of Diarrhea, One Missed Diagnosis

patient.key: 3 years of watery, foul-smelling, oily diarrhea + heartburn responsive to pantoprazole

diagnosis: Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome (gastrinoma — autonomously secreting tumor, duodenal or pancreatic origin)
setting: Office → should have been Inpatient Unit

missedDiagnosis.why: THE diagnostic test. Gastrin >1000 pg/mL (10x upper normal limit) is diagnostic of ZES. This patient had gastrin of 1,200.
Locate the gastrinoma nodule. After biopsy: benign gastric metaplasia. This is the definitive structural diagnosis.
Staging. Gastrinomas can be malignant and metastasize to liver/lymph nodes. Must check before surgery.

missedTreatment.why: Gastrin drives massive parietal cell acid output. PPI blocks the H+/K+-ATPase pump — the final common pathway — regardless of how much gastrin is screaming upstream. Without acid control: ongoing peptic ulcer disease, esophagitis, secretory diarrhea.
Sporadic gastrinomas are CURABLE by surgical resection. This is not a chronic medical management case — it's a surgical one if the tumor is resectable.

missedPerioperative.why: Patient is heading to surgery. Pre-op labs are standard of care — bleeding risk, blood availability, cardiac clearance.

missedMEN1Screen.why: 25% of ZES is associated with MEN1. If MEN1 is present, the surgical approach changes: multifocal disease, harder to cure, usually managed medically. Screening is mandatory before surgery.

missedPreventive.why: Patient smokes cigars 2x/week. Smoking worsens peptic ulcer disease and delays healing. Every office visit is a preventive care opportunity.

timing.note: 1 negative patient update before correct treatment

locationSequencing.note: Wrong location (Office) at Day 2+10:20; should have been Inpatient Unit

mechanismsForImage.title: The Patient Before
mechanismsForImage.concept: 45M musician, healthy, eating, normal life — before the tumor began

mechanismsForImage.title: The Tumor
mechanismsForImage.concept: Gastrinoma in duodenal wall or pancreas, autonomously secreting gastrin into portal circulation

mechanismsForImage.title: Parietal Cell Bombardment
mechanismsForImage.concept: Gastrin molecules binding CCK-B receptors on gastric parietal cells → relentless H+/K+-ATPase activation → massive HCl secretion into gastric lumen

mechanismsForImage.title: Secretory Diarrhea
mechanismsForImage.concept: Acid flood reaches duodenum/jejunum → Na+/H2O absorption fails → high-volume watery diarrhea. Acid inactivates pancreatic lipase → undigested fat in stool (steatorrhea)

mechanismsForImage.title: Bile Salt Precipitation
mechanismsForImage.concept: Low intestinal pH precipitates bile salts → no micelle formation → fat malabsorption → foul-smelling, oily stools (malabsorptive component)

mechanismsForImage.title: Diagnosis: Gastrin Level
mechanismsForImage.concept: Blood draw → serum gastrin 1,200 pg/mL (>10x normal). Below: GI endoscopy finding duodenal nodule, biopsy showing benign gastric metaplasia

mechanismsForImage.title: PPI Blockade
mechanismsForImage.concept: PPI molecule binding irreversibly to H+/K+-ATPase proton pump on parietal cell apical membrane → acid secretion blocked regardless of gastrin levels

mechanismsForImage.title: Surgical Cure
mechanismsForImage.concept: OR table — laparoscopic resection of duodenal gastrinoma. Curative for sporadic ZES. Pre-op CT abdomen (staging) showing no liver mets

mechanismsForImage.title: Recovery and MEN1 Screen
mechanismsForImage.concept: Patient recovered, symptom-free. PPI weaned. Labs panel: PTH, ionized Ca, prolactin. Follow-up CT surveillance. Smoking cessation counseling
